subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw models status --probe --all — per-model health check across all configured models

question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in `models status --probe --all` configured-model live probe now, and what scope/output contract should it own versus fallback-chain and staged-migration diagnostics?
rationale: The feature gap is source-proven, but this adds a new live provider/auth CLI mode that can consume tokens, hit rate limits, and overlap with other model-safety workflows.

options.title: Add narrow `--probe --all` mode
options.body: Implement the requested opt-in status mode for configured models only, with provider/profile filtering, JSON docs, bounded concurrency, and redacted real-provider proof.

options.title: Fold into broader model diagnostics
options.body: Keep this issue as design input while a single fallback-chain or staged-migration diagnostic workflow owns all model health checks.

options.title: Defer live per-model probing
options.body: Leave current auth-profile probing unchanged and ask users to rely on `models scan`, runtime fallback errors, or external scripts until provider-health policy is clearer.

recommendation.title: Add narrow `--probe --all` mode
recommendation.body: Implement the requested opt-in status mode for configured models only, with provider/profile filtering, JSON docs, bounded concurrency, and redacted real-provider proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is provider/auth CLI product direction, and steipete has the strongest recent history across provider identity, auth health, and model status/probe behavior.
